title: At the Movie Theater
goal: Choose a showing, buy tickets, ask about seating or access, and discuss the movie afterward.

runs.text: is a scheduled presentation of a movie.
also works for a movie; you do not have to replace it in every sentence.
Use this fictional listing in Practice:

rows.text: 100 minutes; two adjacent seats available in row D

runs.text: Theater 1 is on the lobby level. Theater 2 is upstairs, with an elevator beside the lobby. The 2 p.m. showing starts in ten minutes in the first practice scene. Ticket prices and buying procedures are not needed for these tasks.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: What time is the next showing of The Hidden Garden?

turns.en: What time is the next showing of The Hidden Garden?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Two tickets, please. Do you have two seats together?

turns.en: Two tickets, please. Do you have two seats together?

runs.text: appear on the screen for the audience.
is another term you may see in listings, especially for dialogue in another language. Ask
What captioning is available for this showing?
if the listing does not answer your need. Do not assume every showing has the same features.
Movie listings in the American MPA system use
signals parental guidance; some material may not suit children.
gives a stronger caution about material for children under thirteen. A rating is not a promise that a particular child will enjoy or be comfortable with the movie.
Is there anything scary in it?
ask different questions about content and entry. This lesson's fictional ratings do not supply a real review of either movie.
Is there time to get popcorn?
asks about a plan before the start. A companion can say
We've got ten minutes. Let's go straight to our seats
Afterward, share an evaluation and let your companion differ:

turns.speaker: Riley

runs.text: The scenery was beautiful, but the story dragged in the middle.

turns.en: The scenery was beautiful, but the story dragged in the middle.

turns.speaker: Alex

runs.text: I liked the slow pace. I thought the ending worked well.

turns.en: I liked the slow pace. I thought the ending worked well.

turns.speaker: Riley

runs.text: The ending surprised me, but I didn't really like it.

turns.en: The ending surprised me, but I didn't really like it.

blocks.caption: Before and after the movie · Alex & Riley

runs.text: suggests it felt slow or boring.
The action scenes blew me away
gives a strong negative opinion. Neither a good nor a bad review requires agreement from the other person.
Speak both roles alone. Use the listing and scene facts above.
Buy two tickets to the next showing of The Hidden Garden at 2 p.m. Ask for seats together. Staff offer the row D pair.

sample.text: Two tickets to The Hidden Garden at two, please. Can we sit together?

runs.text: Ask about Night Train at 3:15. Staff say it is sold out. Ask about and choose the later showing, or decline.

sample.text: Is there space at seven instead? — Yes. — Then I'll take two tickets for that showing.

runs.text: Choose The Hidden Garden's open-caption showing. Confirm the time and ask for the elevator to its floor. Staff answer from the scene facts.

sample.text: Is the five o'clock showing open-captioned? Where's the elevator?

runs.text: Change the need: you are considering a movie for a child and want information about frightening content. Ask that question rather than equate the rating with guaranteed suitability. Staff answer
I don't have a detailed content description here
; choose to find more information before deciding.

sample.text: Is there anything scary in it?
I'll check the content before choosing.

runs.text: There are ten minutes until the 2 p.m. showing. Suggest popcorn; the other person wants to go straight to the seats. Respond and agree on a plan.

sample.text: Let's get popcorn. — I'd rather go to our seats. — Okay, let's do that.

runs.text: Hide the models. Re-create a ticket exchange with one unavailable choice. Then describe one thing you liked and one you disliked about an imagined movie; a companion disagrees with one opinion.

sample.text: I loved the scenery, but the story dragged. — I liked the slower pace.

runs.text: Did the chosen showing still have tickets? Did your question identify the particular access or content information you needed? Could you give a real opinion without requiring the other person to share it?
